Dysfunction of cortical inhibitory circuits in stiff-man syndrome
S.D. Kim, S. Vucic, M.C. Kiernan, V.S.C. Fung (Sydney, New South
Wales, Australia)
Objective: To assess the pathophysiological mechanism underly-
ing clinical features in Stiff man syndrome (SMS) using novel
threshold tracking TMS techniques.
Background: SMS is a rare autoimmune disorder characterised by
persistent stiffness with superimposed episodic muscle spasms.
Although dysfunction of GABA-ergic inhibitory circuits have been
established in SMS, the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying
the development of symptoms remain to be fully elucidated. The
function of GABA-ergic circuits may be assessed clinically using
transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS). Speciﬁcally, the function of
cortical GABA A intracortical circuits is indicated by short interval
intracortical inhibition (SICI), as measured by the paired-pulse para-
digm, while the integrity of GABA B circuits is reﬂected by the corti-
cal silent period (CSP) duration. Using the constant stimulus paired-
pulse TMS technique, motor cortex hyperexcitability was reported in
SMS. However, the relationship of cortical hyperexcitability with
clinical manifestations of SMS remained obscure.
Methods: Cortical excitability studies were undertaken in 2 SMS
patients, using a 90 mm circular coil, and results were compared to
62 normal controls. SICI was assessed with the conditioning stimulus
(CS) intensity set to 70% of resting motor threshold (RMT), while
CSP duration was assessed with stimulus intensity set to 140% RMT.
Motor evoked potentials were recorded over the abductor pollicis
brevis muscle. SMS disease severity was assessed using the distribu-
tion of stiffness index and heightened sensitivity scale.
Results: SICI was signiﬁcantly reduced in SMS patients compared
to controls (averaged SICI patient 1, -0.36%; patient 2, -4.8%; con-
trols, 10.6 60.5%). In addition, CSP duration was signiﬁcantly
reduced in SMS patients compared to controls (patient 1, 116 ms;
patient 2, 106 ms; controls, 210.2 63.1 ms). The extent of SICI and
CSP reduction was greater in patient 2, who exhibited more severe
disease.
Conclusions: These ﬁndings suggest that both GABA A and
GABAB cortical circuits are dysfunctional in SMS, and that this dys-
function in inhibitory circuitry may underlie the development of clin-
ical features in SMS. As such, the threshold tracking TMS technique
may be an important aid in monitoring disease severity and response
to therapy in SMS, especially in clinical drug trials.
